source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details
payment to vendor's bank account on record

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent is instructed to update the vendor record whenever an invoice shows new bank details, with no instruction to independently verify the source of those details before acting. This makes the agent a direct executor of whatever bank details appear in attacker-reachable invoice content.

The sole stated safeguard for irreversible payment and bank-change actions is a human approval of a one-line summary, explicitly optimized for the clerk to 'approve quickly.' There is no structural destination confirmation, raw-action review, or spend limit backing this instruction.

elements.name: Scheduled payment instruction to vendor's bank account
ERP vendor master record (including bank details)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model's one-line natural-language summary, never the bank account number or change history, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from a stronger model can get a fraudulent bank change or payment approved (ASI09). At roughly 150 approvals per day the gate is also subject to approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Hard per-transaction and daily aggregate spend cap (recommended)
Out-of-band callback verification of new bank details (recommended)
Raw-action approval card showing bank account number and change history (recommended)

findings.title: Summary-gated bank detail fraud via fake supplier invoice (TC9)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled supplier portal upload claims new bank details for a known vendor.
Agent matches the invoice to the vendor master record and purchase order.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details directly from invoice content per prompt.md:2, with no independent verification.
Agent schedules payment to the newly stored (fraudulent) bank account on the due date.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version used by the agent changes without a separate review of the approval-card generation logic, or the clerk-approval step is disabled, bypassed, or converted to auto-approve below a threshold.

evidence.observation: Instruction directs the agent to update the vendor record directly whenever an invoice shows new bank details, with no independent verification of the source of those details.
The only control before an irreversible payment or bank change is approval of a one-line summary, explicitly framed to let the clerk approve quickly.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The card shown to the clerk displays only a plain-language summary ('Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187...') with no bank account number and no indication that bank details were just changed.
The card shows only the model's summary; account numbers and change history are not shown, and the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (broad, not least-privilege).

recommendations.action: Require independent out-of-band verification (for example, a callback to a phone number already on file, not one supplied by the invoice) before accepting any change to vendor bank details.
Show the clerk the raw bank account number, the old vs. new values, and full transaction detail on the approval card, not just a one-line natural-language summary.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege, separate vendor-master write access from payment scheduling, and require dual control for bank detail changes.
Add a hard per-transaction and daily aggregate spend cap on scheduled payments, with amounts above the cap requiring a second approver.

findings.title: No attributable, tamper-evident record of bank-detail changes or payment approvals

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of the vendor or payment scope (new ERP modules, new payment rails) is deployed without first adding a tamper-evident, raw-action audit record separate from the approval summary.

evidence.observation: The approval card does not show bank account numbers or change history, and no audit log or action-provenance store is described anywhere in the artifacts.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The retained artifact of the approval decision is a one-line natural-language summary, not the underlying transaction or bank-detail-change record.

recommendations.action: Persist an immutable, tamper-evident record of every agent action distinct from the human approver identity, including full invoice content, prior and proposed bank details, and the system's full reasoning, not just the approval summary.

findings.title: No spend cap or rate limit on scheduled payments under high-volume summary approval

forecast.watch_signal: Model/platform version changes without review, or the clerk-approval step is removed, bypassed, or converted to auto-approval, removing the only per-transaction check on payment volume.

evidence.observation: The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, and no spend cap, per-transaction limit, or daily aggregate limit on scheduled payments is described.
Payment is scheduled automatically on the due date once approved, with no stated maximum amount or frequency limit.

recommendations.action: Introduce a hard spend cap and rate limit on cap.schedule_payment that holds regardless of approval volume.
Separate bank-detail changes and high-value payments into a low-volume review lane distinct from routine invoice approvals, to reduce consent fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates to the ERP system (service account, mTLS, etc.) or whether the agent's identity can be spoofed when invoking ERP tools; no auth method is documented.

The agent cannot modify its own configuration or prompt (can_modify_own_config: false); the only tampering vector in this design is the vendor master write, scored on el.ds_vendor_master and in finding f1.

No capability in this design moves vendor master or bank data outside the trust boundary as a byproduct of the agent process itself; the only egress is the payment itself, assessed under el.flow_payment_egress.

Artifacts do not describe supplier portal authentication or any mechanism attributing an uploaded invoice to a specific verified external account, so non-repudiation of the submitting party cannot be assessed.
This is an inbound flow carrying supplier-authored invoice content into the agent; it does not carry confidential organizational data outward, so outbound disclosure does not apply to this flow.
Artifacts do not describe any invoice volume throttling, rate limiting, or queuing behavior for the supplier portal, so resilience to invoice flooding cannot be assessed.

Payment amount and routing data sent to the vendor's bank is the intended function of the payment itself, sent to the party named in the transaction, not an unauthorized disclosure path distinct from the fraud scenario in f1.
cap.vendor_read is used only internally for invoice-to-vendor-and-PO matching; no capability in this design reads vendor master data and sends it outside the trust boundary.
No capability in this design (read, configure) can delete or lock the vendor master record; a delete action is not defined, so this agent cannot threaten the store's availability.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted supplier-submitted invoice can, per the agent's own instructions, directly cause an irreversible configure action (bank detail change) and an irreversible spend action (payment) with no step or runtime limit declared. The only present control, a clerk approval gate, is a model-summary review under high daily volume (~150/day), which the rubric credits one tier and caps above 'moderate', giving a residual of high. The forecast is critical because that same gate is partially dependent on model capability and review framing: a model upgrade or removal of the gate (both plausible, undeclared-review changes per the runtime notes) eliminates the only credited control and returns the finding to its critical inherent level. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.clerk_approval, specifically because it reviews a model-generated summary rather than the raw action at high volume (ASI09, SAFE-T1403).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or ERP integration/IAM configuration was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact ERP credential scope and whether any destination or duplicate-vendor checks exist) is inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, which lowers confidence on the credential-scope and provenance findings to medium.
No logging, audit trail, or SIEM configuration was described; the repudiation finding (f2) assumes the absence of a control the artifacts do not mention, recorded at confidence: medium.
